newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania gives president power to use troops.
newsitem.headline: Albania gives president power to use troops.

text.p: Albania's parliament on Sunday handed special powers to President Sali Berisha to use troops to guard roads and government buildings after violent protests spread around the Balkan state.

Thousands of protesters, angry over the collapse of pyramid investment schemes, clashed with riot police in Tirana. Albanian television said disturbances occurred in another 13 towns, mainly in the south, where a concentration of people have poured their savings in the investment funds.
Courts, prefectures, headquarters of the ruling Democrats and town halls were set ablaze in a number of towns, television said.
"The president of the republic will be able to apply the decision (empowering him to use troops as guards) as head of the armed forces," Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu told Reuters.
"This decision has nothing to do with a state of emergency but the traffic, water depots, oil reserves, town halls...and strategic sites should not be attacked," he added.
The use of the powers would be temporary and limited for a so-far unspecified amount of time, parliament said.

Parliament, sitting for the first time on a Sunday since Berisha's ruling right-wing Democratic Party swept to power in a 1992 general election, took the vote in an emergency session after demonstrators set scores of buildings ablaze, mainly in towns in the south, and clashes in Tirana.

Parliament is mainly made up of Democrats after they won most seats in a general election last May. The poll was boycotted by the main opposition parties after they accused the Democrats of rigging the vote.
Shehu blamed the growing crisis on what he called "extremist forces".

"It is not the mass of Albanian Socialists, but there are some Marxist extremists who have always wanted to seize power through violence," Shehu told reporters after the vote. "These are segments of the former secret police who want to profit from this moment when Albanian citizens are having financial difficulties to try to destabilise Albania."

Witnesses earlier saw two military trucks carrying about 40 soldiers arrive at the interior ministry in central Tirana. Soldiers armed with sub-machine guns were already on guard around the main Skanderbeg Square where several government buildings are sited.
Interior Minister Halit Shamata called on Albanians to distance themselves from troublemakers.
"Police forces have been very calm but some of the citizens have provoked them and even beaten them," Shamata told state television.

"I beseech people not to join such groups and I want to make clear to everybody that the security forces are determined to ensure the law is observed and they will act according to the law," he added.
Around 30 people had been arrested, he added.
Shamata said some 84 police officers around the country had been injured on Sunday, some seriously. He gave no figures for the number of protesters hurt in the clashes.
